text:
Great teachers never stop learning, and new AI models can help. Here’s how ⬇️

UMD researchers developed M-Powering Teachers, an AI module that delivers more personalized support for both educators and students. Using recordings and transcripts of lessons, a team spanning the College of Education, College of Information, and Clark School of Engineering partnered to analyze this information in collaboration with a certified education coach.

Typically, educators receive feedback only once or twice a year, but the M-Powering Teachers program offers ongoing support for continuous learning. By integrating educational theory, machine learning, language processing, field experiments, and more, M-Powering Teachers provides a dynamic platform dedicated to enhancing the effectiveness of modern education.

text:
Ryan Collins ’16, MBA ’20 was on his way home from a training ride, the gritty kind that made him feel like he could conquer the world. After spending the past couple of years racing up the ranks from a junior mid-Atlantic cycling champion to one of the top riders in the nation, he’d just received his dream phone call: an invitation to try out for the Olympic training team representing the U.S. in Tokyo. His bags were packed, and he was scheduled to fly out to the camp the next morning.

The next thing he knew, he and his bike were crumpled on the ground as onlookers’ screams pierced the air. In a flash, an approaching car had collided with him head-on.

Paramedics rushed Collins to the hospital, where doctors who recognized the elite athlete in their care reluctantly delivered the news: Not only was he not flying out in the morning to the Olympic training camp, but the odds were that he’d never ride a bike again.

“And I’m thinking, ‘Well, just watch me,’” Collins says. 

Now, nearly a decade after the accident, he's breaking records as an ultracyclist, racing for six to 12 hours at a time and winning national and European championships. 

More on his remarkable journey: go.umd.edu/233p

🏈🏑⛳ Cheer on our Terrapins: Join the action to cheer on Terps Football throughout the fall and also grab free student tickets to most other Terps sports: go.umd.edu/freesports25 

❤️🖤🤍💛 Wear your Terp Pride: Take part in our Maryland Friday traditions by proudly wearing red, black, gold, or white to end each week!
